scope: Tranche 0 — two live bugs in the Zig backend: release tag ordering and silent sudo escalation

fixes.defect: updateIsAvailable() fell back to 'any difference is an update' unless BOTH versions were purely numeric-dotted, offering downgrades (installed 1.7.4 stable with forge latest 1.7.4-rc1; installed 2.0.0-rc1 with forge latest 1.9.0).
fixes.fix: New module orders forge release tags: numeric core comparison plus SemVer prerelease precedence, and returns null for tags it cannot order so the historical fallback survives for ETags and calendar tokens.
fixes.regression_proof: With the original logic restored, exactly 4 new tests fail and every pre-existing test still passes — the change is strictly additive.
witness_tests: updateIsAvailable: a release is never offered its own prerelease
updateIsAvailable: prereleases of the same release order among themselves
updateIsAvailable: refuses downgrades across differing cores
parse_github_response: a stable release never downgrades to its own prerelease
guard_tests: parse_github_response: a maintenance release on an old branch is not offered as an update (already handled by the old code; kept as a guard)

fixes.defect: findElevator() scanned PATH for doas/sudo/run0 and defaulted to 'sudo'. The repository AGENTS.md forbids sudo, su, doas and equivalent privilege-bypass tools and requires pkexec/polkit. The violation was invisible because the Rust UI injected SHELLY_ELEVATOR=pkexec into the child environment.
fixes.fix: No implicit PATH scan. SHELLY_ELEVATOR still wins as an explicit operator choice (including run0); the default is now pkexec.
fixes.behavioural_impact: None on this host: run0's auto-detection was already unreachable because sudo shadowed it in the old precedence.

known_gaps: The de-escalation path in Shelly.PackageManager/src/aur/builder.zig (invokingUserCommand) still shells out to `sudo -u <user>` when SUDO_USER is set. It only runs from an already-elevated context and never escalates, so it is out of scope here, but it remains a sudo invocation.
The Rust UI still injects SHELLY_ELEVATOR=pkexec. It is now redundant with the backend default; the comment was corrected rather than the behaviour changed.
